items: Lead AI model development for AI-Hab, a NERC-funded University of Lincoln–UKCEH collaboration; curated an analytical dataset of over 5,000 expert-labelled photographs across 18 fine-grained UKHab-aligned habitat classes from a source pool exceeding 10,000 UKCEH Countryside Survey images.

Designed reproducible training and evaluation pipelines comparing nine convolutional and vision-transformer models; the best reached 71.5% top-1 and 90.9% top-3 accuracy, comparable to the strongest of three experienced ecologists on a stratified held-out subset.

Led the formal analysis and first-author paper in Ecological Informatics, examining class imbalance and habitat-level errors; contrastive learning raised class-specific recall by six percentage points for Improved Grassland and five for Neutral Grassland.

Extended AI-Hab beyond image-only assessment with a multimodal system combining imagery, geospatial data (Google Satellite Embeddings) and LLM-derived ecological descriptions; internal results show a two-point top-1 gain over the image-only baseline.
Released public code, trained models and a public demonstrator; co-organised the 2025 stakeholder workshop involving Defra and Mozaic Earth.
Developed LLM-based multi-agent decision-support methods for Pezego, a mobile pest-management tool for agronomists and farmers, and led the resulting preprint.
Delivered laboratory sessions and student workshops and assessed coursework across Machine Learning, Adaptive Intelligence, Text Processing and Natural Language Processing.
